Ratecard
Quick start guide

Your first better price in ten minutes.

Ratecard is a single file that runs in your web browser. There is nothing to install, no account to create, and none of your numbers ever leave your computer.

1

Save the file Ratecard.html somewhere you will find it, like your Documents folder.

2

Double-click it. It opens in Chrome, Safari, Edge, or Firefox, on desktop or phone.

3

Start at Floor rate. Your inputs save automatically in that browser.

The five modules, in the order to use them

01 Floor rateThe minimum you can charge and still hit your income after tax, expenses, and unbillable time. Watch the utilization trap chart: most people overestimate billable hours.
02 Value pricingEstimate what the project is worth to the client, discount it for uncertainty, and get a fee range with the client's ROI at each price.
03 ProposalBuild Good, Better, Best packages. Use "Price tiers from step 02" to fill them, follow the anchoring check, then save as PDF.
04 Change orderWhen a client asks for more, enter the request and hours. Copy the ready-made message and send it.
05 PlaybookTen tactics with word-for-word scripts: raising rates, handling "too expensive," retainers, and more.

Three moves that pay for Ratecard on your next project

  1. Never quote your floor. Quote at least 25% above it, so you have room to trade scope instead of discounting.
  2. Always send three options. Design the middle one to be chosen, and price the top one to make it look sensible.
  3. When scope grows, send a change order the same day. A small paid change protects the whole relationship.

Saving a proposal as PDF

In the Proposal tab, click Print or save as PDF. In the print dialog, choose "Save as PDF" as the destination. Only the proposal prints; the editor stays hidden.
